Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2a) demonstrates an enlarged main pulmonary artery and a relative paucity of vascular markings in the right lung field, suggestive of reduced blood flow. The axial CT image (Figure 2b) shows calcification within the vessel wall at the origin of the right pulmonary artery (indicated by the arrow), which is characteristic of chronic inflammation and stenosis seen in Takayasu arteritis rather than an acute embolism.
